subject.title: Feature request: config option to suppress transient tool error warnings

question: Should OpenClaw add a normal-chat tool-error delivery policy beyond the existing `messages.suppressToolErrors` boolean, and what safety semantics should it use for failed mutating tools after success-looking replies?
rationale: The remaining work changes public config and user-visible failure delivery: it can improve hosted chat UX, but it can also hide real failed mutations that the current policy intentionally surfaces.

options.title: Approve default-compatible policy
options.body: Add a documented current-default `all` mode plus explicit `final` and/or `off` modes after tests prove failed mutations are not silently confirmed.

options.title: Keep the boolean path
options.body: Treat `messages.suppressToolErrors` as the supported operator opt-out and narrow this issue to docs or channel-specific bugs.

options.title: Split remaining leaks first
options.body: Defer the enum and handle channel-specific leaks, read-only exec classification, or lifecycle-warning routing in separate issues.

recommendation.title: Approve default-compatible policy
recommendation.body: Add a documented current-default `all` mode plus explicit `final` and/or `off` modes after tests prove failed mutations are not silently confirmed.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the merged acknowledged-warning fix and explicitly scoped this issue as the remaining broader policy decision.
